patients.label: 50 year old previously healthy man resuscitated from ventricular fibrillation and diagnosed with Brugada syndrome

identity_evidence.quote: Here, the authors present what they believe is the first reported case of Brugada syndrome presenting as nocturnal enuresis in an adult.
A 50 year old, previously healthy man

attribution_limitations: The authors suggest, with hedged wording, that the nocturnal enuresis resulted from urinary incontinence caused by self-terminating ventricular fibrillation episodes during sleep.
The first enuresis episode is described only as waking to find enuresis; the next sentence calls the additional episodes nocturnal enuresis.
At 0447 h scopes the successful resuscitation; the number of defibrillations and the epinephrine have no stated time of their own.

The Figure 1 ECG strips carry device-printed clock labels (visual record only). The strip the caption calls the restored-circulation column is labelled minutes before the text time of 0447 h for successful resuscitation, so the text resuscitation fact is review_only. The VF strips are labelled after the 0436 h arrival time, which is consistent with persisting VF and is not a differing value for the arrival. The caption refers to columns while the image shows stacked strips.

The text says the patient was transferred to the emergency department and also refers to hospital admission, without stating that these are the same event; the day of admission is not dated beyond September 2013 for the transfer.
The ICD insertion has no stated date. It precedes the May 2015 ICD shock only because that shock was delivered by the device; its order against the diagnosis, hypothermia or extubation is not stated.

evidence.quote:

Electrocardiogram recorded by emergency responders showing ventricular fibrillation.After electrical shocks were delivered (the first column) and epinephrine was administered, spontaneous circulation was restored (the last column).
